title: latency-fingerprint-across-cuda-and-cloud-variants
content:
Purpose:
Quick investigative notes on cross-cloud / cross-driver latency fingerprints for our inference runtime. This doc collects observed deviations, hypotheses, and a minimal reproducibility matrix so we can triage tail behaviors before the Dedicated rollout next quarter.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Under identical workload shapes (prefill + decode, short and long contexts) we see consistent p50/p95 ordering across SKUs but large p99 divergence tied to specific driver+CUDA combinations.
- H100 variants (cloud-specific SKUs) give best sustained throughput for long-context streams but show higher burst tail when GPU P-states or thermal governors kick in under sustained decode.
- A100 instances show more predictable tail latency across driver variants but higher per-token average latency for large attention windows compared to H100.
- L40S (where available) has competitive small-batch latency and lower kernel-launch variance, making it attractive for low-latency small-scale endpoints.
- CUDA/driver pairings matter: CUDA 12.x + driver 535-like stacks produce sporadic kernel enqueue stalls on some EC2 placements; fallback to CUDA 11.8 stacks reduced these particular stalls in our repro.

Test matrix (minimal reproducibility set):
- Models: 7B-llama-style (FP16), 13B-llama-style (FP16).
- Sequence lengths: short (32 prefill + 32 decode), medium (128+128), long (2048 prefill + 512 decode).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4 (microbatching), 16 (throughput mode).
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 concurrent requests.
- Cloud SKUs sampled: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100), AWS hpc6a/h100 variants (where available), GCP a2-highgpu (A100), GCP h100 (a future preview SKU), Azure NDv5 (H100), and NVidia L40S-enabled marketplace images (where available).
- Driver/CUDA matrix: CUDA 11.8 + driver 520, CUDA 12.0 + driver 525, CUDA 12.1/12.3 + driver 535. Also test with the OS-level nvidia-persistenced on/off.

Instrumentation/measurement notes:
- Use internal microbench harness (perf-runner v0.9) with eBPF-based kernel-launch tracing and per-token timestamping forwarded to trace collector.
- Measure p50/p90/p95/p99/99.9 for prefill and decode phases separately.
- Capture GPU metrics: SM utilization, power draw, clocks, NVLink utilization, PCIe counters where available.
- Collect driver logs (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q -x) at start/end and when a tail event is observed.
- Ensure workload pins CPUs to isolated cores so host jitter is minimized.

Representative findings (raw-ish):
- Short context (32+32), batch=1, concurrency=1:
  - A100 (CUDA11.8/driver520): p50=18ms p95=25ms p99=35ms
  - H100 (CUDA12.0/driver525): p50=16ms p95=30ms p99=60ms (sporadic long tail ~200ms on ~0.1% of calls)
  - L40S (CUDA12.1/driver535): p50=19ms p95=26ms p99=32ms
  Notes: H100 shows better median but heavier p99; L40S very consistent for small token counts.

- Long context (2048+512), batch=4, concurrency=8:
  - A100: sustained per-token decode throughput lower (~5%) than H100 but tail was flatter (p99 ~ 1.8x p95).
  - H100: higher sustained throughput but p99 spikes when clocks drop under thermal pressure (p99 ~ 3.5x p95).

- Driver effects observed:
  - CUDA12.1 + driver535 on several GCP A100 placements produced intermittent kernel enqueue waits (~100-400ms). Reverting to 11.8 stack eliminated the long enqueue waits in our replay runs.
  - Enabling nvidia-persistenced reduced startup variance on machines with cold worker pools but didn't eliminate mid-run stalls attributed to PCIe/DRAM refresh cycles.

Hypotheses and triage notes:
- Hypothesis A: H100 thermal/P-state transitions under sustained decode lead to transient clock drops causing kernel hangs at the enqueue or increased queue latency.
  - Triage: instrument GPU clocks and pstate change logs while forcing high clocks (coolbits boost) in lab to see if tails disappear.

- Hypothesis B: Newer driver stacks schedule different kernel launch/stream priorities (CUDA runtime changes) which can expose race conditions in our continuous-batching layer causing occasional stall.
  - Triage: run with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and set explicit stream priorities; add extra ordering fences in a debug build to see if stalls reduce.

- Hypothesis C: Some cloud placements have root complex/PCIe path differences that increase DMA latency variability (we saw correlation with specific AZs).
  - Triage: correlate at AZ level and compare PCIe counters; repro by migrating instances to different placement groups.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to confirm whether Linux kernel versions (5.x vs 6.x) correlate strongly with the enqueue stalls — gather node kernel version metadata in next runs.
- Are any of these effects visible at application-level traces we ship to customers? Create a short alert rule to flag >150ms single-token decode events in hosted API logs.
- Validate whether quantization (INT8) changes the tail characteristics (we only tested FP16 here).

Quick action items (for next 2 weeks):
- Miguel: create a minimal repro job that reliably triggers the ~200ms H100 tail (attach exact kernel call stack when observed). Link: JIRA-INF-987.
- Priya: run the same matrix on a batch of instances pinned to the same AZ on AWS and GCP (n=5 each) and capture PCIe counters + driver dmesg.
- Ava: add a debug build of runtime that inserts optional extra stream-fencing to isolate ordering-related stalls; run with CUDA12.1/driver535 to confirm impact.

Notes to self (scribbles):
- We should avoid immediately concluding "H100 is flaky" — need to map to placement/driver stacks. Some fast paths on H100 are clearly higher throughput at cost of susceptibility to transients.
- Consider expanding the matrix to include mixed-tenant noise (co-located VMs) since cloud interference might amplify tail in production.

Appendix: useful commands and short logs to attach when filing bugs:
- nvidia-smi dmon -s u --interval=1
- sudo cat /var/log/nvidia/driver.log (where present)
- dmesg | grep -i nvrm
- perf-runner command used: perf-runner run --model 7b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --concurrency 8 --trace eBPF --outdir /tmp/perf-a100-run1

References / links:
- GH PR with harness changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1670000000000000
- Jira: JIRA-INF-987 (H100 tail repro)

If anything looks off or you have local placement IDs that correlate, paste them here and I'll tie them to the telemetry blobs.

-- Ava
